GLOBAL-DQ-043.reason: the sport contests men and women in one field, so a mixed stage is one open to both rather than one requiring both, and a national team is picked on merit. GLOBAL-DQ-066.reason: the Comp.Rank half of the same fact, and the sharpest form of it: every one of the 44 team rankings the sport holds is reported, because no rule here requires a team's genders to balance. The proportion is the finding.

GLOBAL-DQ-067.reason: asserts that a lineup holding both genders holds them in equal number, which the sport does not require: 2040 of its 2818 mixed lineups are uneven. The proportion is the finding, and a shift in it would be worth reading.

GLOBAL-DQ-004.reason: the template requires a stage's dates to equal its first and last event dates, and this sport does not store them that way: a stage is written as whole days, 00:00:00 to 23:59:59, so a stage containing every one of its events still differs from their span by the hours at each end. The template's own prerequisite excludes a checkpoint split by name, and the sport has no RESULT_FINAL_SCORE_TYPE_ID for it to compare against.

GLOBAL-DQ-086.reason: it reads a per-period score against an approved vocabulary of numbers and sentinels for a period that was not played. The value shapes those columns do carry are audited at event level by Swimming-DQ-039 and Swimming-DQ-047.

GLOBAL-DQ-091.reason: it asserts that every participant of an event stores every period the event contests, reading them from SCOPE_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_LIST. Swimming's scope layer is checkpoints, not periods: a distance marker with a time, not a segment of the contest that scores. The question the check asks does carry over to a split layer - whether the same checkpoint is recorded for every swimmer in the race - but the structure it reads to ask it is not the one this sport stores, and a signal is read off the structure. Recorded as considered and rejected on 2026-08-20 rather than left unclassified, because it is the one of the five that is not obviously inapplicable.

GLOBAL-DQ-092.reason: it orders periods by ascending data type id and checks that a not-played sentinel never precedes a scored period. Swimming stores no per-period score and no such sentinel, so SCOPE_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_LIST and SCOPE_PERIOD_SENTINEL_LIST both have nothing to name. Its checkpoint ids do ascend with the race, but there is no sentinel whose position could be wrong.
